rationales: Solid particles dispersed in a gas form an aerosol, not mist.
Gas dispersed in liquid describes a foam, not mist.
Mist consists of tiny liquid droplets dispersed in a gas.
Gas dispersed in a solid is a different type of colloid.
Methane is nonpolar and is not appreciably soluble in water.
Sodium chloride dissolves readily in water to form ions.
Ethene is nonpolar and is not appreciably soluble in water.
Benzene is nonpolar and is not appreciably soluble in water.
Benzene does not produce ions in solution and is a non-electrolyte.
Hydrogen chloride ionizes in water and conducts electricity.
Sodium hydroxide dissociates into ions in water and is an electrolyte.
Acetic acid partially ionizes in water, so it is a weak electrolyte.
Protons are charged and are less penetrating than neutrons in matter.
Electrons are charged and are less penetrating than neutrons in matter.
Neutrons have no electric charge and are the most penetrating choice listed.
Alpha particles are strongly ionizing and have low penetrating power.
C₆H₁₂O₆ is the molecular formula, not the simplest ratio.
CH is not the simplest whole-number ratio of glucose's atoms.
Dividing the glucose formula subscripts by six gives CH₂O.
C₆H₆ is the formula of benzene, not glucose.
Eight grams of CO₂ is about 0.18 mol, not 0.15 mol.
The amount is 8 g ÷ 44 g mol⁻¹ ≈ 0.18 mol.
Eight grams of CO₂ is not 0.21 mol.
Eight grams of CO₂ is not 0.24 mol.
The long-form periodic table is arranged by atomic number, not Mendeleev's postulate.
Elements in the long-form periodic table are arranged in order of increasing atomic number.
Atomic mass is not the modern basis for arranging the long-form periodic table.
Mass number is not the basis for arranging the periodic table.
Hydrogen has the lowest molar mass listed, so it diffuses fastest.
Helium is lighter than the other choices except hydrogen, but heavier than hydrogen.
Fluorine gas has a greater molar mass than hydrogen and diffuses more slowly.
Chlorine gas has the greatest molar mass listed and diffuses most slowly.
NH₃ has a complete octet around its nitrogen atom.
BF₃ has only six electrons around boron, making it electron deficient.
Each nitrogen in N₂ attains an octet through a triple bond.
Each oxygen in O₂ attains an octet through a double bond.
A covalent bond pair contains more than one electron.
A covalent bond pair consists of two shared electrons.
Three electrons do not constitute a bond pair.
Four electrons are not the number in a single covalent bond pair.
Chalk does not dissolve in water and its particles can settle, so it forms a suspension.
Chalk particles in water are not a stable colloidal dispersion.
A solution is homogeneous, whereas chalk remains undissolved.
Chalk is the dispersed solid, not the name for the whole mixture.
Sulphur is generally dull, not lustrous.
Phosphorus is generally not lustrous.
Iodine crystals have a characteristic lustrous appearance.
Carbon is not generally lustrous in its common non-metal forms.
Isotopes are forms of an element with different numbers of neutrons, not different physical forms.
Allotropes are different physical forms of the same element.
Amorphous describes a solid without long-range crystal order.
Crystalline describes a solid with an orderly structure, not different forms of one element.
A concentrated solution of common salt in water is called brine.
Benzene is a separate organic compound, not salt water.
Alcohol is not the name for concentrated salt water.
Toluene is a separate organic compound, not salt water.
Opal is not a liquid dispersed in a gas.
Opal is not a solid dispersed in a gas.
Opal is commonly classified as a solid-in-solid solution.
Opal is not a gas dispersed in a solid.
